scope: quantitative cerebral blood flow from a 2D multislice pCASL dataset with background suppression and a separate M0 scan
time_expectation: designed to be completed within a 60-minute working session on a CPU-only laptop

input_files.asl.npz: key 'asl': float32 [n_volumes, n_slices, ny, nx] magnitude images of the pCASL series in acquisition order; volumes alternate between control and label (see acq.json 'first_volume'). Array index order is [volume, slice, row, column].
input_files.m0.npz: key 'm0': float32 [n_slices, ny, nx] proton-density (M0) images acquired with the same 2D multislice readout and receiver gain as the ASL series, without labelling and without background suppression, with repetition time acq.json 'm0_tr_s'; each slice was excited only once per TR (no preparation pulses).
input_files.t1.npz: key 't1_s': float32 [n_slices, ny, nx] tissue longitudinal relaxation time T1 in seconds from a separate T1 map co-registered to the ASL grid (0 outside the head).
input_files.acq.json: acquisition parameters for this dataset (keys listed under acquisition_parameters).

acquisition_parameters.label_duration_s: pCASL labelling duration (bolus duration) in seconds
acquisition_parameters.pld_s: post-labelling delay in seconds, defined as the time from the end of labelling to the excitation of the FIRST ACQUIRED slice
acquisition_parameters.slice_order: list of slice indices (0-based, index into the slice axis of the arrays) in the order in which they were acquired after each labelling/control period
acquisition_parameters.slice_interval_s: time between the excitations of consecutively acquired slices
acquisition_parameters.labeling_efficiency: pCASL labelling (inversion) efficiency at the labelling plane, not including any effect of background suppression
acquisition_parameters.n_bs_pulses: number of background-suppression inversion pulses played between the end of labelling and the excitation of the first slice
acquisition_parameters.bs_inversion_efficiency: inversion efficiency of each background-suppression pulse for arterial blood magnetization
acquisition_parameters.m0_tr_s: repetition time of the M0 acquisition in seconds
acquisition_parameters.first_volume: 'control' or 'label': type of volume 0 of asl.npz; types then alternate
acquisition_parameters.partition_coefficient_mL_per_g: whole-brain blood/tissue water partition coefficient lambda in mL/g

physiology_conventions: Single-compartment kinetics: the labelled water decays with blood T1 after the label is created (consensus white-paper assumption); all arterial transit times are shorter than the PLD of the first acquired slice; the labelled bolus has a rectangular shape of length label_duration_s. Images are noise-corrupted; noise is additive Gaussian before the magnitude operation and the SNR is high. There is no subject motion and no partial-volume mixing between voxels.
endpoint: voxel-wise cerebral blood flow in mL/100 g/min on the input grid [n_slices, ny, nx]
accuracy_targets: On hidden datasets with different acquisition parameters, slice orders and noise realizations: for every slice, the mean CBF over grey-matter voxels must be within 6% of the true grey-matter mean, and the mean over white-matter voxels within 10% of the true white-matter mean. The same targets apply to the public dataset. Voxels outside the brain are not scored.

entrypoint.cli: python asl_cbf.py --input-dir <directory containing asl.npz, m0.npz, t1.npz, acq.json> --output <path ending in .npz>
entrypoint.standalone: all custom code must be inside this one file; installed third-party packages may be imported. It must run in a clean directory containing only this file and the input directory, reading every acquisition parameter from acq.json (hidden datasets have different values, matrix sizes and slice orders).

output_schema.cbf: float [n_slices, ny, nx] CBF in mL/100 g/min on the input grid; any value outside the brain

entrypoint.runtime_limit: each run of the entrypoint (public or hidden inputs) must finish within 15 minutes on one CPU core with single-threaded numerical libraries

required_outputs: cbf.npz (the entrypoint run on the public inputs)
environment.txt (Python version and package versions; environment.json or requirements.txt also accepted)

report_output_schema.model: string describing the quantification model and every correction applied
report_output_schema.effective_labeling_efficiency: float used for the public dataset
report_output_schema.pld_by_slice_s: list of the post-labelling delay used for each slice index of the public dataset
report_output_schema.gm_cbf_by_slice: list of your mean grey-matter CBF per slice (use your own segmentation or thresholds)
report_output_schema.validation_summary: string or object describing how you checked the result

deliverable_location: place the deliverables at the workspace root or in one subfolder
grading_note: The grader reads cbf.npz, reruns asl_cbf.py with the workspace .venv interpreter on the public inputs and on hidden datasets, and compares slice-wise grey- and white-matter means with ground truth.
